items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine, Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine and Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1959-02-27
items.q: I go to Cascaro's house and get these tuba. Called the gentleman, you come on out here. Now get in this band. Here, play this.

ctx.x: Let me tell you a little story about the Chinamen. I had them on bass pedal and had them on guitar all the time, you know. And it seemed like I needed more tuba players. I only had two at the time, you understand? Then I got Lawyer Cannon, May Street, and I had to get five tuba players anyway. So, here comes young Buffalo Bill, a fellow by the name O'Brien, for the Wild West Show. Well, they found out about me, you understand? They come down to shame me. And I had Cascaro on tuba. items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1964-04-25
items.q: So we played, went down the corner, we played, went back to the lot. ... It was a fellow by the name of O'Brien, young Buffalo Bill. Young Buffalo Bill. Yes, he had that show.

ctx.x: Yeah. You were going to tell us about the Wild West show?

Yes. Well, this is a coincidence that happened to me. I had a man, young man, playing tuba. His name was Joe Cascaro. And one day he took seriously sick. Now that evening he sent me word that he wasn't able to come down to play music with me and play us at this Wild West showcase. Well here I wasn't a terrible fix. Well a friend of mine, I thought of the Chinaman, Martin. I runs up to Casco and I borrow his tuba. And I give the tuba to this boy to play. He said to me, I don't know nothing about... I said you…
This was a marching band? Marching band? Marching band. Marching band.
